name: kafka-observability
description: LangSmith-parity observability over Kafka for any LangGraph.js / LangChain.js agent. Ships a vendored src/observability/ library — a BaseTracer subclass that captures EVERY traced run (graph, nodes, LLM calls with full prompts/outputs/token usage, tool runs, errors, trace hierarchy) exactly as LangSmith receives it, and publishes each run as start/end events to a Kafka topic over a bounded, non-blocking, fire-and-forget producer (librdkafka, acks=all, idempotent). Disabled by default (KAFKA_ENABLED). By default EVERY run is emitted; an opt-in, payload-verified run filter (KAFKA_RUN_FILTER_MODE allow/deny + run_type:name globs, name side also matching metadata.langgraph_node, root run always emitted) lets an app drop verified-duplicate wrapper events to cut volume with no information loss. The /add-kafka-observability skill installs OR upgrades the library in a target repo: detects pre-existing Kafka functionality first (foreign src/observability/ modules, producers elsewhere) and asks the user to classify it — agent-flow observability (keep-both or replace with downstream sign-off) vs unrelated (always preserved) — never overwriting a foreign module; then vendors the module, adds the client dependency, wires one startup() call at the graph entrypoint (dual global attachment — configure hook plus the configure-slot LangSmith's own tracer occupies, robust to platform runtimes that sever async-context ancestry; no per-node instrumentation), updates .env.example and deployment settings, and verifies with typecheck + unit tests. Intake proposes broker/topic/security defaults discovered from sibling repos in the workspace that already carry the library (propose-only; the user confirms every value). Runs alongside LangSmith so it can be validated in parallel before LangSmith is unplugged.
